newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL small-cap stocks end with strong gains.
newsitem.headline: KL small-cap stocks end with strong gains.

text.p: Retail buyers piled into small-capitalisation Kuala Lumpur shares on Friday, while blue chips settled nearly flat amid a dearth of institutional participation.
"The interest today has been mostly on the Second Board by the retail market," said Irene Tan, head of research at Vickers Ballas. "Technically, it is very attractive."

After hitting an intraday high of 593.66 for the year, the Second Board index ended at 592.83, up 15.99 points or 2.77 percent. The blue chip-focused Composite Index touched a high of 1,232.56 for the day before ending at 1,231.45, up 0.92.
"Many institutional investors are still on vacation," said Matthew Geiger, head of research at Phileo Allied. "There's nothing compelling to get them back into the market yet."
He added, "The local market is being affected by the volatility of the Dow at the moment."
The Dow, which dropped about 100 points on Tuesday, ended six points lower on Thursday after recouping from a 96 point dive.
At day's end, over 147 million shares had traded, compared with 88 million on Thursday. Gainers topped losers by 385 to 214.
